rq: joint identification of raw language equivalence and latent intervention partition
primary_work: Bianchi et al., Language in a (Search) Box: Grounding Language Learning in Real-World Human-Machine Interaction, NAACL 2021
decision: NARROWED BEYOND INTERACTION-DERIVED CLICK DENOTATION — NOT ADOPTED
reason: Real user-machine interaction and clicks as noisy pointing signals already support empirical lexical denotation and compositional grounding without explicit semantic labels. However, the interaction channel may inherit semantics from the serving policy, catalog, exposure mechanism, and metadata; observational clicks do not identify latent intervention effects; and simultaneous query/target/serving-interface recoding can preserve the complete observed interaction law and all reported retrieval metrics while changing raw-language equivalence, target partition, or denotation.
surviving_candidate: After recovering the finest raw-expression equivalence available from legitimate language-only observations, the finest target partition identifiable from legitimate non-language interventions, and the strongest denotation learnable from non-random user-machine interaction, determine whether a preregistered cross-system intervention law uniquely resolves only the remaining exposure- and response-aliased classes while eliminating every query/target/serving-policy recoding preserving the complete language, exposure, click, causal, and outcome laws.
public_baseline_reproduction: not started; paper-declared repository returned 404 through connected GitHub API and no immutable commit or reproduction bundle was available
